volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: CONEY ISLAND
notes: New York City's summer resort located in Brooklyn which is 10 miles from the city. Nearly 6 miles long and 1 mile wide. This is perhaps the most popular playground in the world and is visited by over 20 million persons during the summer. Here one will find all kinds of amusements that are spectacular to old as well as the young. All subways and bus lines serve this section as well as steamboats to Steeplechase Pier.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: GEORGE WASHINGTON BRIDGE
notes: Spanning the Hudson to Fort Lee, N. J. It is the longest suspension bridge in the world. The length of the bridge and its approaches (including the tunnel to Amsterdam Ave.) is 12,430 ft. The span across the river is 3,500 ft. The view from this bridge is magnificent as you can view the shores of New York and the Palisades of New Jersey.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: METROPOLITAN MUSEUM OF ART
notes: Building contains 38 galleries and rooms to foster the study of fine arts and the practice of applied art. Open daily 10 A. M. to 5 P. M. except Sundays, Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Years when the hours are 1 to 6 P. M. Admission Free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: LA GUARDIA AIRPORT
notes: The main artery of air transportation for New York is actually located within the city limits of Long Island. Hundreds of airliners arrive and depart daily to and from all sections of the United States, South America, England and all parts of the world. Admission to the promenade deck is 10c.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: STATUE OF LIBERTY
notes: Visitors admitted free 9 A.M. to 4 P.M. Oct-April, 9 A.M. to 5 P.M. May and Sept, 9 A.M. to 6 P.M. June-Aug. Boats from Pier A, Hudson River, Fare 35c.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: WHITNEY MUSEUM OF AMERICAN ART
notes: Open daily 1 to 5 P.M., Sat/Sun 2 to 6 P.M. Closed Mondays, July 4th, Thanksgiving, Christmas. Admission Free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: MUSEUM OF THE NUMISMATIC SOCIETY
notes: Hours: 2-5 Daily and Sundays. Closed July 16 to September 1. Free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: NEW YORK MUSEUM of SCIENCE and INDUSTRY
address: R. C. A. Bldg., Rockefeller Center
notes: Hours: 10 A.M. to 10 P.M. every day. Adults 25c, Children 10c.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: NEW YORK BOTANICAL GARDENS
notes: Hours: 10 A.M. to 5 P.M. daily, free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: AMERICAN GEOGRAPHICAL SOCIETY
notes: Hours: 9 A.M. to 4:45 P.M. Closed Sundays and Holidays and on Saturdays during the summer.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: HAMILTON GRANGE
notes: Hours: 10-5; Saturdays 10-1. Closed Sundays and Holidays. Free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: THE THEATRICAL DISTRICT OF NEW YORK
notes: Where all of the largest and best plays are staged and produced, is located in the heart of the city.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: CATHEDRAL OF ST. JOHN, THE DIVINE
notes: America's greatest church edifice. When completed it will be the largest Gothic Cathedral in the world. The seating capacity is 15,000 and room for 40,000 standing.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT NATIONAL HISTORIC SITE
notes: Dedicated as national historic one on January 15th, 1944. It comprises 33 acres. Open to visitors from Tuesday to Saturdays, inclusive and Sundays and holidays (including any holidays that fall on Monday) from 10 A. M. to 5 P. M. Admission 25c.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: CITY HALL
address: Broadway, Park Row and Chambers Streets
notes: Seat of government of the metropolis; can be visited by the public from 10 A. M. to 4 P. M. daily.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: THE GENERAL POST OFFICE
address: 31st St. to 33rd St. and from 8th to 9th Ave.
notes: Largest post office in the world; houses 18,000 employees, makes 26 collections and 3 to 4 deliveries a day.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: HOLLAND TUNNEL
address: Starts at Canal St. in New York and ends at 12th St. in Jersey City, N. J.
notes: Underwater link under the Hudson River; consists of 2 tubes, ventilated by 84 fans.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: NEW YORK ZOOLOGICAL PARK
notes: Has the greatest collection of animals in the world; occupies 264 acres. Open 10 A. M. to one-half hour before sunset. Admission free except Tues., Wed. and Thurs. Charges: Adults 10c and Children 5c.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: CENTRAL PARK
address: 5th Avenue and Central Park West, 59th to 110th Streets
notes: The largest park in the city; contains 862 acres, a Zoological Park and many playgrounds.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: PENNSYLVANIA STATION
address: West 31st and 33rd Sts. between 7th and 8th Aves.
notes: Main station of the Penn. system in the city; one of the finest terminals in the world.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: ELLIS ISLAND
address: Upper bay of New York harbor
notes: First landing place of the immigrant; may be visited by securing a pass from the Commissioner of Immigration.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: MUSEUM OF THE CITY OF NEW YORK
notes: Hours: 10 A. M. to 5 P. M., Sundays 1-5 P. M. Closed Tuesdays. Free except Mondays 25c.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: GOVERNOR'S ISLAND
address: Upper part of New York Bay
notes: Important military headquarters and headquarters of the Eastern Division of the U. S. Army. Passes required to visit from an officer at the Barge office.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: THE EMPIRE STATE BUILDING
notes: Tallest building in the world; 102 stories above ground, 2 stories under ground. Houses more than 25,000 tenants.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: GREENWICH VILLAGE
address: West of Washington Square and south of 13th St.
notes: Famous for its nightclubs, restaurants, artist studios, antique furniture and art shops. Many are housed in old barns, lots and cellars. The Village is still a place of gay and unconventional night life.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: FRICK COLLECTION
notes: Hours: Sundays and Holidays 1-6. Closed Mondays, Decoration Day, July 4th and Christmas. Free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: MUSEUM OF THE AMERICAN INDIAN
notes: Hours: 2-5. Closed Sundays, Holidays and through July and August.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: THE HAYDEN PLANETARIUM
address: American Museum of Natural History at 81st Street and Central Park West
notes: There can be seen "The Drama of the Skies." The most interesting feature is the "Hall of the Sun," which shows the Solar System. Hours: Weekdays shows at 2, 3:30 and 8:30 P. M.; Sat. 11 A. M., 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8:30 P. M. Sundays and Holidays 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8:30 P. M. Admission Matinees 30c, evenings 40c, Children (under 17) 20c at all times.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: AMERICAN MUSEUM OF NATURAL HISTORY
notes: Hours: 10 A. M. to 5 P. M. Sundays 1-5 P. M. Free.

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: GRANT'S TOMB

volume_title: The Negro Motorist Green Book: 1948: A Classified Motorist & Tourist Guide Covering the United States & Alaska
name: HARLEM
address: between 110th and 155th Sts., bounded by Eighth, Park and Lenox Aves.
notes: The greatest Negro metropolis in the world where over 300,000 colored people live. Here you will find a city in itself: fine restaurants, taverns, nightclubs and department stores.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: CATHEDRAL OF ST. JOHN THE DIVINE

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: CENTRAL PARK
address: 59th to 110th Sts. & Fifth Ave. to Central Park West
notes: Zoo in southeast corner. Fifth Ave. Bus Nos. 1 to 6, 9 & 19; Broadway-Seventh Ave. Subway to Columbus Circle; Broadway bus to 59th St.; 6th and 7th Ave. bus to 59th St.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: CHINATOWN

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations

address: Fort Tryon Park, north of George Washington Bridge
notes: Collection of medieval art. Open daily except Mondays from 10 A.M. to 5 P.M. Free except on Fridays. Fifth Ave. Bus No. 4; Eighth Ave. subway 190th St.-Overlook Terrace Station.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: EMPIRE STATE OBSERVATORIES
notes: 1,250 feet above. Open 9:45 A.M. until Midnight.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: GEORGE WASHINGTON BRIDGE
address: spans the Hudson between 178th St. in Manhattan and Fort Lee, New Jersey
notes: Longest suspension span in the world except Golden Gate Bridge, California. Roadway is 12 stories or about 250 feet above the water. Total cost $60,000,000. No. 4 Fifth Ave. Bus. No toll for pedestrians.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: GOVERNOR'S ISLAND

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: HALL OF FAME

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: HALL OF MOTION (N. Y. Museum of Science and Industry)

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: METROPOLITAN MUSEUM OF ART
notes: Open daily 10 A.M. to 5 P.M. Sundays 1 to 5 P.M. Admission free. Fifth Ave. Buses Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4. Madison Ave. Bus Nos. 1, 2. Lexington Avenue Subway to 86th St. Station.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations

Sundays, 1 P.M. to 5 P.M. Holidays, 10 A.M. to 5 P.M. Free at all times. Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4 Fifth Ave. Buses; 103d St. Station Lexington Ave. Subway; Madison Ave. Bus Nos. 1 and 2.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: UNITED NATIONS
address: Manhattan Island, 42nd to 48th Streets; between 1st Avenue and the East River
notes: Visitors are always welcome; all but a few of the meeting places are open to the public. Admission FREE. Free tickets are issued upon request to the Council, Commission or other bodies in session. Guided Tours through thes Headquarters Building and other exhibits; a small fee is charged. Buildings are open at 9 A.M. Can be reached by the 42nd Street bus.

volume_title: The Negro Travelers' Green Book: 1955 International Edition: The Guide to Travel & Vacations
name: TRINITY CHURCH
notes: The present building is the third on this site and dates from Ascension Day, May 21, 1846. I.R.T. 7th Ave and Lexington Ave. Subways, Wall St. Stations.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: Statue of Liberty
notes: Bartholdi's huge female figure of 'Liberty Enlightening the World,' presented to the United States by France in 1885. Figure, 151 ft. tall, tops 142 ft. pedestal. The copper statue alone weighs 225 tons. Circular stairway of 168 steps leads to interior of head. Boat to island leaves Pier A, Battery Place on the hour daily.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: United Nations World Capital
address: Along the East River, north of 42d St.
notes: Houses the Secretariat which is the 3,000-employee administrative organ of the United Nations, staffed by international civil servants. Meeting place of the General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council and Trusteeship Council. For guided tour consult the Admissions Office.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: CHINA TOWN
notes: A short walk from City Hall and Brooklyn Bridge. Joss houses, curio shops and Chinese restaurants.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
name: TIMES SQUARE
address: Intersection of Broadway, Seventh Ave. and 42nd St.

volume_title: Go, guide to pleasant motoring, Vol. 1
